question: A spell that would destroy my creature is already resolving -- it's actually destroying the creature right now. Can I activate a regeneration ability in response, before the creature is actually put into the graveyard, to give it a regeneration shield in time?
workedSolution: A player can activate an ability to regenerate a creature in response to a spell that would destroy it. Once the spell resolves, though, it’s too late to regenerate the creature.

whyHard: Regeneration is a replacement effect, and replacement effects must be in place before the event they modify actually happens -- they can never reach back in time. A player can regenerate a creature only in response to the spell that would destroy it, i.e. before that spell resolves; once the destroy effect has already resolved, no regeneration shield created afterward can undo it.
